description: The registered process returns an accepted job receipt in data.job_id and data.status=queued. Retain that exact canonical id and read service_interface::job_service::get_job until terminal. The stored job.result is the original operation envelope, including data and structured error; job.error is also retained on failure. A receipt does not establish a session or a successful first turn. launch_busy names the current operation/job and starts no work. It starts a session from the solet's own concepts only: the caller, runtime, model and effort, a workspace directory, the first message, permissions and an opaque label. agent_runtime, model, effort, workspace and first_message are required. workspace is the absolute path of an existing directory, used verbatim as the session's working directory, and nothing is created in it. first_message is non-blank text delivered byte for byte as the session's first turn. label is opaque text stored on the session and returned by list_sessions and session_status, never parsed, and may be empty. The permission arguments (permission_mode, allowed_tools, allow_askuserquestion) and host, visibility, local_name, report_by_seconds, transport, provider_env, degraded_hooks_acknowledged and spawned_by_instance_id are optional; permission_mode and transport fall back to plugin.yaml, and allowed_tools is the explicit list, else plugin.yaml's default_allowed_tools, else empty. Any other argument is refused as unknown at submission. The calling session's identity, when the call carries one, is recorded as lineage (spawned_by_instance_id), else the caller's own spawned_by_instance_id argument; a caller with neither still starts, with empty lineage. Refusals, all at submission before any job or ledger row exists: generic_spawn_field_required (agent_runtime, model, effort or first_message blank), generic_workspace_invalid (workspace relative, missing or not a directory), host_not_declared, host_mechanism_missing and model_cell_disabled (a model cell policy rule turned the named runtime/model/effort cell off; the message names the rule). A cell the model capability catalog does not know still starts, with a model_cell_unknown entry in data.advisories. The terminal job result carries agent_instance_id, agent_runtime, host, host_ref, lifecycle_state, first_turn_delivered, first_turn_error, label, workspace and advisories. On the claude_code tmux host first_turn_delivered=true means the first_message was handed to the CLI as its launch prompt, which the CLI submits itself when ready; on every other host it means the driver channel accepted the text. Writes the managed_session ledger row in 'spawning' state BEFORE dispatching through the host driver, so a half-failed spawn stays visible rather than silently disappearing. Three host drivers ship: 'operator' (degenerate, observes via registration only, never spawns), 'headless' (D1 — spawns an actual Claude Code process over stream-json, config-gated fail-closed on a resolved permission mode/.mcp.json/the claude binary), and 'tmux' (D2 — spawns a detached tmux session running the interactive claude CLI, config-gated fail-closed on the tmux binary/version plus the same claude-launch checks as headless; its spawn() also runs a bounded PTY-confirm expect loop for the interactive --dangerously-load-development-channels prompt, fail-closed on timeout). Host choice affects deploy survival: a 'headless' worker is swap-mortal by construction (a direct child of the platform process, killed unconditionally on every platform stop including a blue-green deploy's quiesce step) while a 'tmux' worker is swap-durable by construction (its pane belongs to the independent tmux daemon, untouched by the platform's stop/swap path) — prefer 'tmux' for any worker expected to outlive a single release; a deploy holding live headless workers needs an explicit quiesce-or-accept decision recorded in the deploy reason. Optional provider_env (an object of environment names to string values) selects the Claude provider backend for this one worker. It is accepted only for runtime claude_code on the tmux host, where it is applied to the pane's own environment on new-session -e; it is refused with provider_selection_not_applied_by_host on the headless and operator hosts, and with provider_unsupported_for_runtime for any other runtime. An overlay key that names a managed worker variable is refused, naming the key only. The values are never written to the persisted job payload, the ledger row, the spawn detail or any log line. Known limit: the values are visible to local process listings (ps) for the instant of the tmux new-session call, as the identity variables already are. Refusals surface as a failed launch job, not at admission, because the overlay is taken out before preflight. A spawn-time PreToolUse tool allowlist mechanism exists (allowed_tools, or plugin.yaml's default_allowed_tools when the call names none) — an out-of-allowlist tool call is denied with a clean error, never executed and never a silent hang — but per operator ruling (2026-08-03, 'we don't have any restrictions now') it ships UNARMED by default: an empty/unconfigured allowlist means no extra restriction, not a lockdown. The permission mode itself (plugin.yaml's headless_permission_mode) similarly accepts any value today; the driver only refuses when no mode resolves at all. The tmux driver denies Claude Code's structured-choice AskUserQuestion tool by default (operator ruling, 2026-08-14 — its blocking picker stalls an unattended or peer-driven session); allow_askuserquestion=true lifts the deny for that one spawn. The headless driver needs no equivalent: measured live, its stream-json mode never enumerates the tool in the first place, so the flag is inert there. The codex runtime has no equivalent tool at all. W6 (#13 §44.3, 2026-08-14): local_name is the name the spawned worker answers to on its OWN machine — the headless driver's --name and the tmux driver's --name plus the label its session name derives from. Omitted, it defaults to the label when one is given, else to the new session's instance id. ROUTING IS A SEPARATE THING, and the distinction matters: having the local name does NOT make peer_send_by_name deliver to that role. Spawning deliberately does NOT claim any durable role binding (operator ruling, 2026-08-14) — claiming a role adds a name and never releases the incumbent's, so an automatic claim at spawn would EVICT whoever currently holds it: a destructive act triggered by a routine one. A spawned worker that needs a role claims it explicitly once it is up. REFUSAL (operator ruling, 2026-08-14): a second spawn under a local_name that a non-terminal managed_session row already holds is refused loudly with local_name_already_held, naming the incumbent's agent_instance_id, lifecycle_state, host and host_ref, plus the terminate_session call that would free the name. Never a silent uniquifying suffix and never a silent eviction. The ordering is terminate the holder, THEN spawn the replacement. HOW THIS RELATES TO THE OTHER TWO ROLE GATES, since an adopter will meet these three in some order and reading only one of them teaches the wrong general rule: (1) THIS verb refuses a second spawn under a live local name; (2) peer_claim_role independently refuses a claim against a LIVE different-session holder with role_held_live, unless an explicit takeover is passed after operator confirmation — that gate already shipped and is NOT new here, so do not build a second one on top of it; (3) a holder that reads DEAD by the liveness window is claimable cheaply, with no explicit terminate, and this is deliberate rather than an oversight: a session that crashed can no longer release its own role, so a gate that also refused dead holders would strand that role permanently behind a session that no longer exists — a worse failure than the collision the refusal exists to prevent. Crash succession stays cheap on purpose. W4A (#8 §43.1, 2026-08-14): degraded_hooks_acknowledged (default false) is the explicit opt-in to spawn onto a host whose preflight can PROVE the worker's hooks will not run — a managed Claude Code policy listing 'hooks' in strictPluginOnlyCustomization strips hooks from every non-plugin source, including the --settings blob both drivers inject worker hooks through. Without the flag such a spawn is refused by host_cannot_spawn, naming the policy file and the offending key. With it, the spawn proceeds, the choice is recorded on the ledger row and logged loudly, and 'running degraded' stays a stated operator decision rather than something discovered later from the silence. At a same-local-name collision, synchronously probe each incumbent exact native host/ref. Only observed dead may transition through the existing legal lifecycle edge with observed_dead rationale, without terminating the host, releasing registration or evicting a role. CAS predicates include the observed host, host_ref, lifecycle_state, last_transition_at and last_heartbeat_at, including nulls. A lost CAS discards the observation, rereads the full same-name set and probes again; new incumbents require fresh evaluation. Alive and unknown/error observations retain local_name_already_held at the duplicate-process integrity boundary, with explicit observation detail. Unobservable operator hosts are unknown. Successful repair is followed by a full requery before replacement; no telemetry-age prerequisite is added.
embedding_description: Start a managed coding-agent session from generic fields: runtime, model, effort, a workspace directory, the first message, permissions and an opaque label. Submits a bounded session-launch job; retrieve its final result by exact job id.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Accepted submission only: data.job_id and data.status=queued. After terminal retrieval, job.result.data carries the original operation fields; job.result.error preserves its error. Continue dependent actions only after this retrieval.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Report acceptance with job_id. Retrieve the terminal job before reporting an instance or its first-turn outcome.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Admission refuses generic_spawn_field_required, generic_workspace_invalid, host_not_declared, host_mechanism_missing, model_cell_disabled and a provider_env refusal before any ledger row is written, and local_name_already_held before dispatch; a host_cannot_spawn after the row is written terminates that row. host_cannot_spawn is the one failure that happens AFTER the ledger row exists — the row is transitioned straight to 'terminated' before the error surfaces, so no spawn is ever left stuck in 'spawning' for a launch already known to have failed. local_name_already_held names the incumbent and the terminate_session call that frees the name; the fix is to terminate the holder and re-spawn, never to add a suffix (a suffixed name is a different name, so the worker would no longer answer to the name it was spawned for). host_cannot_spawn also carries the managed-policy refusal: when the host's managed Claude Code policy lists 'hooks' in strictPluginOnlyCustomization, the worker's hooks cannot run and the spawn is refused by name rather than producing a worker that answers turns while never registering. Set degraded_hooks_acknowledged to proceed anyway; it is recorded on the row.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: generic_spawn_field_required: agent_runtime, model, effort or first_message was blank. generic_workspace_invalid: workspace was relative, missing or not a directory. model_cell_disabled: the named runtime/model/effort cell is turned off by the model cell policy rule the message names. host_not_declared: an explicit blank host override was passed. host_mechanism_missing: the resolved host (override, FLEET_SESSION_HOST env, or the 'headless' default) has no driver registered in this build at all — none of 'operator'/'headless'/'tmux' matched, most likely a typo'd host name. host_cannot_spawn: the resolved driver is registered but cannot spawn right now — the 'operator' driver never spawns (degenerate by design), or the 'headless'/'tmux' driver is registered but unconfigured (missing permission mode / .mcp.json / the claude binary, or for tmux an unsupported tmux version — the error names exactly which). An unknown-argument refusal names the undeclared argument and the declared ones.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For generic_workspace_invalid, pass the absolute path of a directory that exists; the spawn never creates it. For model_cell_disabled, name an enabled cell (read_model_cell_policy lists them) or change the named rule with set_model_cells_enabled. For host_mechanism_missing, pass a host name that is actually registered ('operator', 'headless', or 'tmux') — there is no other name to wait for; check for a typo. For host_cannot_spawn against 'headless' or 'tmux', fix the exact configuration gap the error names (permission mode, MCP config, the claude binary, or the tmux binary/version); against 'operator', launch the session manually instead — this verb cannot do it for that driver.
